# Sample hourly rate build-up

Builds a made-up hourly rate from a base rate, add-on percentages and a fee, one step at a time. Every rule and number in it is invented to exercise the calculator template.

This is a static calculator. It is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with its
reference values bundled in. It runs entirely in the browser: there is no
server, nothing is stored, nothing is sent anywhere, and it works offline.

## What this tool does not cover

- Every rule, rate and threshold here is fictional. Do not use the result for a real proposal, invoice or contract.
- It covers one labour category at a time and does not add travel, materials or other direct costs.
- It does not check whether a rate is allowable under any real regulation.

## Use it

Open `index.html` in a browser, or serve this folder with any static file
server.

## Check it

Every worked example is a saved set of inputs with the exact results that must
come out.

- In a browser: open `tests/index.html`.
- With Node.js: `node tests/run.js` (no packages, no network).

Worked examples in this repository:

- The starting values: 40.00 an hour, 100 hours, standard fee tier
- A high rate on the high-risk tier, where the fee cap applies
- A low rate, where the minimum billable rate applies
- The lowest values allowed: nothing an hour and no hours
- A rate chosen so that the fringe lands exactly on a half: 0.20 an hour

## Sources

1. Sample Rule 12.3(a) (fictional). Sets the made-up fringe percentage (https://rules.example/sample-rule-12-3)
2. Sample Rule 12.3(b) (fictional). Sets the made-up overhead percentage and what it applies to
3. Sample Rule 12.4 (fictional). Sets the made-up fee tiers and the cap on the fee
4. Sample Rule 12.5 (fictional). Sets the made-up minimum billable rate

## Security

Each page carries this content security policy, and whoever serves the folder
should send the same value as a `Content-Security-Policy` header:

    default-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; form-action 'none'

The pages load nothing from another site and contain no tracking or analytics.

## Files

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `index.html` | The calculator. |
| `data/tool.json` | The calculator's definition: inputs, fixed values, lookup tables, steps and sources. |
| `js/data.js` | The same definition as a script, so the page also works when opened straight from disk. |
| `js/decimal.js`, `js/engine.js` | Exact decimal arithmetic and the step-by-step calculation. |
| `js/app.js` | Connects the page to the calculation. |
| `tests/` | The worked examples and the two ways to run them. |
| `moldloft.json` | What generated this repository, and the SHA-256 of every file in it. |

## How this repository was made

It was generated by Moldloft v0.1.0-draft from a build specification and the
`calculator` stack template. No AI model ran. The same specification always
produces these same bytes. Do not edit the files by hand; change the
specification and generate again.
